quizzes.title: California Motorcycle (Class M) Practice Test #1
quizzes.description: California DMV Class M motorcycle license practice test #1. Real questions covering helmets, lane position, braking, cornering and group riding.

questions.question: Helmets are required to be worn by:
options: Passengers only.
All motorcycle riders and passengers at all times.
No one when driving on city streets.
questions.explanation: California law requires all motorcycle riders and passengers to wear a U.S. DOT compliant helmet at all times when the motorcycle is in motion.

questions.question: Grabbing the front brake or jamming down on the rear brake:
options: Can cause the brakes to lock.
Is the best way to stop in an emergency.
Is the best way to slow down when streets are wet.
questions.explanation: Suddenly grabbing the front brake or jamming the rear brake can cause the brakes to lock and lead to a skid. Apply both brakes smoothly and firmly.

questions.question: Motorcycle passengers should:
options: Put their feet on the ground when stopped.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit as far forward as they can without crowding the operator, with both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: Riding in a staggered formation when in a group:
options: Is recommended at all times.
Should not be used when entering or exiting a highway.
Should be used when riding on curves.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is recommended for straight roads, but when entering or exiting a highway or riding through curves, riders should move to single-file formation.

questions.question: Eye protection:
options: Is not needed if your motorcycle is equipped with a windshield.
Is only needed in bad weather.
Should give a clear view to either side.
questions.explanation: Proper eye protection must give a clear view to either side. A windshield is not a substitute for eye protection.

questions.question: The primary cause of single-vehicle motorcycle collisions is:
options: Driving too fast for weather conditions.
Running wide in a curve and colliding with the roadway or a fixed object.
Running off the road to avoid other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Most single-vehicle motorcycle crashes occur when riders run wide in a curve and collide with the roadway or fixed objects.

questions.question: The best lane position for a motorcycle:
options: Is in the left part of the lane, next to the center line.
Is in the right part of the lane, next to the curb.
Can vary depending on road and/or traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Riders should adjust their lane position based on changing road, traffic, and weather conditions.

questions.question: When riding at night you should:
options: Move closer to the vehicle ahead to use its lights.
Keep your normal speed to avoid being hit from behind.
Reduce your speed because visibility is harder at night.
questions.explanation: Visibility is reduced at night, so reduce your speed, increase your following distance, and use the headlights of cars ahead to help see the road.

questions.question: The motorcycle engine cut-off switch should be used and the clutch squeezed when:
options: The throttle is stuck and you can't free it.
You start to lose control in a curve.
The motorcycle starts to wobble.
questions.explanation: If the throttle sticks and you cannot free it, use the engine cut-off switch and squeeze the clutch to stop the engine from driving the rear wheel.

questions.question: Which class of driver license is required to operate a moped?
options: Class M1
Class M2
Class C
questions.explanation: A Class M2 license is required to operate a moped or motorized bicycle. A Class M1 license is required for a regular motorcycle.

questions.question: Upshifting or downshifting in a curve:
options: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the curve.
Is the best way to control your speed.
questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before entering a curve. If you must shift in a curve, do so very smoothly because sudden shifts can cause the rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:
options: Increase the following distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you if you are being tailgated.
Make sure your turn signal turns off after you finish a turn.
Use your horn only in emergency situations.
questions.explanation: Always check that your turn signal turns off after completing a turn. A signal left on can mislead other drivers about your intentions.

questions.question: A major factor in motorcycle collisions is:
options: Following too closely.
Lane sharing.
Not being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: The most common cause of motorcycle crashes with other vehicles is that motorists fail to see the motorcycle. Make yourself visible with bright clothing and proper lane position.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wander while crossing metal bridge gratings, you should:
options: Downshift immediately to a lower gear to improve traction.
Proceed in a zig-zag pattern until you cross the bridge.
Relax, stay on course and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Metal bridge gratings cause the motorcycle to wander. The safest response is to relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.question: When carrying a load on a motorcycle, it should be:
options: Either over or in front of the rear axle.
Carried on the gas tank in front of the driver.
Piled up against a sissy bar or frame on the back of the seat.
questions.explanation: Loads should be kept low and either over or in front of the rear axle. Loads placed behind the rear axle can affect how the motorcycle turns and brakes.

questions.question: Grabbing the front brake or jamming down on the rear brake can:
options: Cause the brakes to lock.
Be the best way to stop in an emergency.
Be the best way to slow down when the streets are wet.
questions.explanation: Grabbing the front brake or jamming the rear brake can cause the wheels to lock and result in a loss of control. Apply both brakes smoothly.

questions.question: The best way to stay out of trouble while riding a motorcycle is:
options: To see it coming by looking well ahead.
By avoiding high density traffic areas.
By increasing the following distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: Search well ahead of you to identify hazards early. The further ahead you look, the more time you have to react and avoid problems.

questions.question: A motorcycle has the advantage over an automobile when passing parked vehicles because:
options: A motorcycle can accelerate faster than a car.
A motorcycle rider can avoid opening door problems by driving in the left part of the lane.
Motorcycles have a shorter stopping distance.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can use the left portion of the lane when passing parked vehicles, which helps avoid being struck by suddenly opening doors.

questions.question: Brightly colored, reflective helmets and clothing:
options: Should only be worn while riding at night.
Can make motorcycle riders easier to see.
Do not increase a motorcycle rider's safety.
questions.explanation: Bright, reflective clothing and helmets make motorcycle riders far more visible to other motorists during the day and at night.

questions.question: To execute a turn safely, you should:
options: Lean the motorcycle in the direction of the curve or turn.
Slow down in the turn.
Turn using the handle bars only.
questions.explanation: To turn, the motorcycle must lean in the direction of the turn. Slow down before entering the turn, then lean and look through the turn to where you want to go.
